threads.body: The JDK gating logic relies on hard-coded string literals (`"8"`, `"11"`) inline, which makes the policy easy to miss and harder to extend (e.g., if additional “exploded-only” JDKs are needed). Consider centralizing this decision behind a small helper (e.g., `usesExplodedSpringBootImage(jdk)`), or at least extracting the supported values into a constant (e.g., a set) so the intent is explicit and the list is maintained in one place.

The new comment explains why JDK 8/11 need a separate pin, but `SPRING_BOOT_VERSION` itself is now implicitly “JDK 17+ (bootJar/executable layout)”. Consider adding a short comment directly above `SPRING_BOOT_VERSION` clarifying that it refers to the executable/bootJar Spring Boot image for JDK 17+ to prevent future confusion when updating these pins.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The current `SPRING_BOOT_VERSION` pin applies to every Spring smoke image from JDK 8 through 25. The image build selects Jib's exploded layout for JDK 8 and 11 and the executable bootJar layout for JDK 17 and newer under that one coordinated tag. A JDK 17+ comment would therefore describe the constant incorrectly.

Upsides: Keeping the existing comment avoids misleading future updates about the scope of the shared pin.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: The image update is the condition explicitly recorded in `PrometheusSmokeTest.java:31-33` for restoring its full JDK matrix, but Java 11 and 17 remain excluded there. That leaves the updated exploded JDK 11 image and the new executable-layout JDK 17 image without Prometheus smoke coverage; please restore `{8, 11, 17, 21, 25}` and remove the temporary comment.
